features.text: The patient has had abdominal pain for about ten days, which has been worsening over the last couple of days, especially after meals.
The abdominal pain is located on the right side, low, and may radiate slightly to the left.
The pain is characterized as a dull ache but can feel sharper when pressed.
The pain is constant but waxing and waning in severity throughout the day.
The pain worsens after meals and with certain positions.
The patient has experienced nausea and some heartburn, but no vomiting.
There has been no change in bowel habits, no fever, and no weight loss.
The patient has no history of abdominal surgeries or gastrointestinal issues.
There is no family history of gastrointestinal diseases.
The patient has not undergone any imaging studies or blood tests for this abdominal pain.
There has been no change in bowel habits, no diarrhea, constipation, or blood in the stool.
The patient has not had any recent changes in diet or consumption of fatty foods.
There has been no recent trauma or injury to the abdominal area.
There have been no changes in the menstrual cycle or gynecological symptoms in the last few weeks.
The patient has not had any recent changes in diet or started any new medications.
There has been no recent weight loss or changes in appetite, and no history of gastrointestinal infections or travel to areas with potential exposure to foodborne pathogens.
